claim.claim_text: Near-surface air temperature over interior and western Alaska has risen
claim.variable: T2M (MERRA-2 2 m air temperature via NASA POWER)
claim.variable_plain: yearly average air temperature about 2 m above the ground

product.name: NASA POWER Monthly API, MERRA-2 T2M (reanalysis model output)

regional.weights: cos(latitude) area weights on cell anomalies

shipped.label: Mann-Kendall with Yue-Wang effective-sample-size correction (lag-1)
shipped.selection: highest power among candidates whose size stayed within 0.05 +/- 2 SE at this series' persistence (STATS_LOG addendum 2)

sen.interval_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance

ols.note: familiar baseline (least squares, t-test); context, not the verdict

band.meaning: slope-range band: the Sen line rotated about its value at the median year between the limits of the 95% slope interval; it does not include uncertainty in the level at the pivot

sensitivity.definition: stable = regional significance-in-direction status identical across coverage thresholds 0.7/0.8/0.9 and interval-excludes-zero status identical across block lengths 1/3/5; this is a sensitivity check, not independent validation

verdict.text: The data support the claim. For interior and western Alaska, annual mean, 1981 to 2025, the yearly average air temperature about 2 m above the ground increased by 0.443 degC per decade (interval 0.19 to 0.628; Mann-Kendall with autocorrelation correction, p = 0.001), which is statistically significant at the 0.05 level. After false-discovery control, 98% of the mapped area is flagged in the claimed direction (a descriptive share, not an error rate). This describes the data over this period; it does not say why it changed or what comes next.

finding.variable: yearly average air temperature about 2 m above the ground

change_per_decade.interval_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance
change_per_decade.interval_meaning: A 95% interval for the Sen slope per decade, built by the method named above. How often such intervals contain the true slope was measured on synthetic series (see the validation results). It is not an interval for individual years

product.name: NASA POWER Monthly API, MERRA-2 T2M (reanalysis model output)

finding.verdict_text: The data support the claim. For interior and western Alaska, annual mean, 1981 to 2025, the yearly average air temperature about 2 m above the ground increased by 0.443 degC per decade (interval 0.19 to 0.628; Mann-Kendall with autocorrelation correction, p = 0.001), which is statistically significant at the 0.05 level. After false-discovery control, 98% of the mapped area is flagged in the claimed direction (a descriptive share, not an error rate). This describes the data over this period; it does not say why it changed or what comes next.
not_supported: It does not say why the value changed, and it does not predict what happens next.
It describes this region, season and period only; it does not apply to other regions, seasons or periods.
It does not test whether the pattern of cells as a whole is unlikely by chance (field significance was not tested).
False-discovery control does not validate any single hotspot and does not measure the share of area that is wrong.
The values are reanalysis model output, not a direct measurement.
finding.selection_disclosure: This headline is the one regional test registered for this claim before any data were downloaded (WP0 claim registration). The region, season and period were not changed after looking at results.
finding.scope_text: The change per decade is for the area-weighted average of the whole region (the containing area), not for any hotspot or single cell. The map shows where individual cells pass the tests; any hotspot value is pointwise and is not adjusted for having been selected.

method_notes: Python is the source of truth; the browser replays these numbers.
Anomalies are computed per cell against its own per-calendar-month climatology over the claim period before any averaging.
Regional series: cos(latitude) weighted mean of anomalies; a region-month needs the coverage threshold of valid cells; a season needs at least two thirds of its months.

Mann-Kendall S and tie-corrected Var(S); Hamed-Rao (1998) correction from Sen-detrended rank autocorrelations with significance-screened lags, factor floored at 1. The correction is less reliable for short series.

Missing years: Mann-Kendall and Sen use valid years only (Sen uses calendar-year differences); Hamed-Rao counts lags in valid-observation order, which treats observations after a gap as adjacent (approximation).
Slope interval and chart band: residual moving-block bootstrap around the Sen line; same draws for both; raw trending values are never resampled.

Benjamini-Hochberg controls the expected share of false discoveries among flagged cells under independence or positive dependence (Benjamini and Yekutieli 2001); spatial correlation alone does not establish that; the rate was measured on correlated synthetic fields. It does not control the share of area that is wrong and does not validate any single hotspot. Flagged-area fractions are descriptive.
Field significance is out of scope. Hotspot-mean intervals, if shown, are pointwise and not adjusted for selection.
Synthetic calibration does not establish that BH is valid for every real field.

cells.cells_mode_note: bh_flags: rung-4 flags are false-discovery controlled (measured on correlated synthetic fields). unadjusted_descriptive: rung-3 flags are UNADJUSTED and descriptive; no false-discovery claim; the verdict does not use the map. off: validation not attached.

cells.rung2_note: With complete months, anomalies only shift each cell's series by a constant, which Mann-Kendall and Sen ignore; rung 2 changes a cell only where months are missing.
cells.flagged_in_direction_def: flag at the rung AND the cell's Sen slope has the claimed sign
